Image URL: https://images.indianexpress.com/2016/10/agnieszka-radwanska-m.jpg# Radwanska’s China Open Triumph

Agnieszka Radwanska clinched the China Open women’s singles title in Beijing with a commanding 6-4, 6-2 victory over Johanna Konta. The Polish star broke Konta early in the first set, weathered a brief counterbreak, and then sealed the opener before dominating the second set with two more breaks and an ace to serve out the match.

This win marked Radwanska’s 20th career title and her third of the 2016 season, achieved without dropping a set throughout the tournament. The victory also echoed her previous success at the Beijing event in 2011. Konta’s run to the final secured her a spot in the WTA top-10 rankings, making her the first British woman to reach that milestone since 1984.

On court, Radwanska held the ornate gold trophy inscribed “Women’s Singles Champion,” her expression a mix of relief and pride. The bright red and gold of the trophy contrasted with her black athletic attire, capturing the celebratory mood of the final in early October.

Image URL: https://assets.tennismajors.com/uploads/2020/09/hingis_graf_roland_garros_1999.jpg# Hingis and Graf Celebrate at the Italian Open

In Rome’s historic Foro Italico, teenage sensation Martina Hingis and long-reigning world No. 1 Steffi Graf pose with their trophies after a thrilling match. Hingis, aged just 15, stunned the tennis world by defeating Graf in the quarter-finals of the 1996 Italian Open, ending Graf’s two-year unbeaten streak on clay. The Swiss prodigy’s tactical brilliance and precise dropshots overcame Graf’s powerful forehand and legendary footwork.

The sunlit clay courts and a cheering crowd set the stage for this landmark upset. Graf claimed the first set 6-2, but Hingis adapted her game plan, winning the next two sets 6-2, 6-4. This victory foreshadowed Hingis’s rise to world No. 1 less than a year later, while Graf would go on to reclaim dominance by winning three Grand Slams and the WTA Championship in 1996.

Image URL: https://d2me2qg8dfiw8u.cloudfront.net/content/uploads/2023/10/01184538/veronika-kudermetova.jpg# Kudermetova’s Tokyo Triumph

Veronika Kudermetova, fresh off her quarterfinal upset of World No. 2 Iga Swiatek, clinched the Toray Pan Pacific Open title in Tokyo. In a final against American Jessica Pegula, Kudermetova displayed relentless fighting spirit, overcoming a 5-5 first-set deadlock and capitalizing on back-to-back double faults to take the opener. She then dominated the second set with powerful returns and two break points, finishing with 17 winners to Pegula’s seven.

The champion’s victory plate—a vibrant red lacquer dish decorated with cherry blossoms and a classical Japanese figure—was kissed in celebration. Kudermetova, who trained as a junior at Moscow’s CSKA club but now holds no formal ties, has secured her second WTA 500 title after Charleston 2021. Her win in Tokyo marks a significant turnaround after early-season struggles and sets a confident tone for the weeks ahead.

Image URL: https://m.thepeninsulaqatar.com/get/maximage/20160908_1473335141-28552.jpg# WTA Elite Trophy Final Celebration

Venus Williams of the United States and Karolina Pliskova of the Czech Republic posed together after the women’s singles final at the inaugural WTA Elite Trophy in Zhuhai, southern China. Williams, dressed in blue, clutched the champion’s ornate heart-shaped trophy and a tournament mascot, while Pliskova, in red and white, held the runner-up’s decorative silver platter.

The final, played on November 8, 2015, ended with Williams defeating Pliskova 7-5, 7-6 (8/6). This victory marked Williams’s second title in as many weeks following her Wuhan Open win and propelled her back into the world’s top 10 for the first time since April 2011. At 35, she became the oldest player to re-enter the top 10 in two decades, concluding the season with three titles—her best haul since 2008.
